findings.quote: can fail badly under a three-meter tower
findings.note: class 4: unit/house-style incoherence. The passage sets fall height in metric ('three-meter') but reports depth loss in imperial ('two inches short of it') with no conversion, and uses US spellings ('meter', 'fiber') throughout; a copy desk standardises one system per piece. Editor's rewrite: 'can fail badly under a ten-foot tower' (with 'two inches' kept) or 'three-metre tower' with 'five centimetres short'.

findings.quote: a bed that met its rating in May may be two inches short of it by September
findings.note: class 3: loose pronoun reference — a bed is short of the depth the rating assumes, not short of the rating itself, so 'short of it' collocates badly with 'rating'. Editor's rewrite: 'a bed that met its rating in May may be two inches below the depth that rating assumes by September'.
